limitation: Quantile scaler flattens time-trending predictors under a temporal split
detail: A QuantileTransformer fitted on training rows maps any test value below the training minimum to 0. Under a temporal split, accrual_days trends with calendar time, so 154 of 156 test games clipped to 0 and the feature became constant - AUC exactly 0.5000. Correct pipeline behaviour with a real consequence for time-trending covariates.

limitation: Retention base rate shifts between train and test
detail: At-risk rate is 33.6% in train and 49.4% in test. The threshold is absolute and fitted on train, while test games are newer with less accrued playtime. Not leakage - train and test pose measurably different problems, which is what a temporal split is for.

limitation: Post-Review Persistence is right-censored at the collection date
detail: playtime_forever is a single snapshot. Persistence is therefore all post-review playtime up to that date, with a censoring window that differs by game age. It is not an early-access-only measure and is not described as one.

limitation: Shared measurement between same-instrument predictors and outcomes
detail: Persistence vs post-launch persistence rho=0.867; EA vs post toxicity rho=0.779. Those pairs share an instrument, so their high AUCs measure trait persistence, not forecasting. The cross-instrument model is the one path free of this.

limitation: Temporal split assertion permits a boundary tie
detail: The assertion uses <=, so two different games launched on the same timestamp could sit either side of the split. Different games, so not leakage, but worth stating.
